exposure: internal manual rotation of the head
outcome: Success rate of internal head rotation
cohort: 152 singleton term (37-42 weeks) pregnancies with persistent intrapartum arrest of the fetal head
finding: Internal head rotation, either manual or digital, was successful in correcting fetal head malpresentation in 80.92% of cases, leading to a higher rate of vaginal deliveries and a lower cesarean section rate.
mod_finding: Internal head rotation, a mode of delivery intervention, was successful in 80.92% of cases and was associated with a higher rate of spontaneous vaginal delivery.
